passage:
A new apartment building had large windows facing an older building. Residents in the older building felt watched.
The developer said the windows gave better light. Residents said light for one building should not destroy privacy for another.
The city required privacy screens and trees between the buildings.
Architecture students studied the case. They learned that design decisions do not stop at property lines. A window creates a relationship.
Good buildings must consider not only the people inside, but also the people nearby.
Privacy is part of comfort. A bright room should not make someone else's home feel like a stage.
